items.title: 67296_Chauncey Morehouse oral history interview
items.q: He was also the model for Dorothy Baker's Young Man With a Horn.

ctx.x: Another article. Only part of the name of the newspaper is evident. 'Press' is the last word, p-r-e-s-s. It says Wednesday, September 27, 1950. "Forest Hills drummer with a boogie beat has played the happy music for 30 years. If the residents of Forest Hills' Ingram Street suddenly hear a Dixieland drumbeat, the sound of a vibraharp, kettledrums or any other percussion instrument, they won't wonder where it's coming from. Chauncey Morehouse, a jazz drummer with almost 30 years of the happy music behind him lives…

He started playing in his high school band in Chambersburg, Pennsylvania. He got his first paid job playing a banjo for Ted Weems in the early twenties. "Ted and I were kids together" Morehouse said, "and he offered me this spot playing banjo. I took it and I was in business". From the Weems band, Morehouse went to various other dance units in the 1920s. Among them, the orchestras of Paul Whiteman, Jean Goldkette and Red Nichols and His Five Pennies. He's played on the same stand with most of the jazz musicians…

all of a sudden." Morehouse met his wife, Evelyn, in 1924 when he was supposed to be preparing to enter the Boston Conservatory of Music, his father's idea. "I was supposed to enter in September," Morehouse said. "I had my choice, marry Evelyn and play jazz music or put it off, study theory and harmony. And we got married in August. That settled it."
